key_insight: SurfPhase reconstructs sharp, deformable liquid–vapor interfaces from sparse video views by representing the interface explicitly and optimizing a differentiable rendering pipeline, enabling accurate 3D interfacial dynamics where prior neural-rendering methods fail.
problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of measuring and reconstructing 3D interfacial dynamics in two-phase flows from limited camera views—classical techniques struggle near moving interfaces and existing neural-rendering methods assume diffuse, single-phase boundaries.
method: Represent the interface using dynamic Gaussian surface primitives (compact, learnable kernels) that can move and deform over time.
Use a differentiable rendering objective to fit sparse multi-view video frames, aligning appearance and geometry while preserving a sharp boundary.
Incorporate physics-inspired regularization (e.g., surface continuity, normal consistency, temporal smoothness) to stabilize reconstruction from sparse observations.
impact: Enables accurate 3D reconstruction of sharp two-phase interfaces from sparse cameras, benefiting experimental fluid dynamics, data-driven modeling, and simulation-to-real transfer by providing high-quality volumetric/ surface training data and diagnostics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → dynamic Gaussian surface model → differentiable rendering → reconstructed 3D interface
Side-by-side comparison: ground-truth video frame vs. rendered reconstruction highlighting a sharp vs. diffuse interface
Time-lapse sequence: evolving 3D surface meshes or iso-surfaces showing interfacial dynamics across frames
Quantitative bar/line chart: reconstruction error or interface sharpness vs. number of input views (sparse → dense)
paper_title: SurfPhase: 3D Interfacial Dynamics in Two-Phase Flows from Sparse Videos
paper_authors: Yue Gao, Hong-Xing Yu, Sanghyeon Chang, Qianxi Fu, Bo Zhu
